identity.title: Detecting the Semantic Fixed Point: A Geometric Framework for Efficient Inference

problem.claim: Determine when Transformer-layer iteration should terminate during inference.

gap.claim: Existing early-exit methods use output confidence as a proxy for internal convergence rather than measuring convergence directly.

contributions.claim: A geometric early-exit criterion based on vanishing normalized update norm and stabilized cosine direction between consecutive hidden-state updates.
The criterion has O(d) per-layer overhead, independent of vocabulary size, and uses neither learned components nor architectural modifications.
The authors report a sharp two-phase structure in layer-wise updates: volatile early changes followed by small, aligned updates.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper proposes directly examining hidden-state trajectory geometry for early exit, instead of relying on output confidence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report 30–35% FLOP reductions on LLaMA-2-7B and LLaMA-2-13B across question answering and commonsense reasoning, while retaining over 98% of full-depth accuracy.
The authors report that layer-wise updates undergo a remarkably sharp transition from large, volatile updates to small, aligned updates.

narrative_sequence.summary: Transformer layers are framed as an iterative refinement process, raising the question of when to stop.
Existing early-exit approaches are described as inferring internal convergence from output confidence.
The authors report a sharp two-phase geometry in hidden-state updates.
They operationalize convergence by jointly checking update magnitude and directional stability.
The authors report substantial FLOP savings with over 98% retained full-depth accuracy on two LLaMA-2 models and two task categories.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a qualitative geometric transition to two measurable signals—normalized update norm and consecutive-update cosine similarity—and then reports task-level compute and accuracy outcomes.

lessons.interpretation: A technical proposal is easier to assess when its mechanism, observable criterion, and outcome metrics are explicitly connected.
lessons.application: Frame a systems method by mapping the claimed internal phenomenon to measurable decision signals, then report both resource savings and task-performance retention.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the proposed internal signal cannot be measured reliably or when task-level outcomes are unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify exit thresholds, calibration procedure, evaluation baselines, or the distribution of exit depths.
The reported results cover only LLaMA-2-7B/13B and question answering/commonsense reasoning tasks; broader scope is unspecified.
